elements.element: The Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York.
elements.evidence: Section 28.1 expressly provides that the Agreement is governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York.

elements.element: The state and federal courts located in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 grants those courts exclusive jurisdiction but permits either Party to seek temporary injunctive relief concerning confidential information or intellectual property in another court. This express exception means New York County jurisdiction is not fully exclusive as required.

elements.element: The Agreement is governed by the laws of Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Section 28.1 selects New York law, not any fallback governing law.

elements.element: Jurisdiction lies with courts corresponding to the selected fallback law—Delaware courts, California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 selects courts in New York County, subject to a limited injunctive-relief exception, rather than any accepted fallback forum.

result.reason: The redline correctly replaces Singapore law with New York law and resolves the prior conflict between Sections 28.1 and 28.2. However, the retained right to seek temporary injunctive relief in another court prevents the New York County courts from having unqualified exclusive jurisdiction, so the complete preferred position is not achieved. No fallback law or forum is selected. Because an additional deletion or qualification of the carveout would be needed to reach a complete accepted position, the redline is not minimal under the stated definition.
